name: Test Suites MCP
description: MCP server that exposes the Darwin test suites as tools: run_integration_suite (IntegrationRun) and run_retrieval_suite (RetrievalRun).

parameters.instructions: Test suite runners plus Slack usage inspection for the Darwin agent. run_integration_suite checks tool routing and tool results through the agent (integration_cases). run_retrieval_suite scores retrieval quality (retrieval_cases). run_consistency_suite scores cross-attempt agreement (consistency_cases). run_agent_integration_suite / run_agent_retrieval_suite run the same cases against the FirstClassDarwin n8n Agent via messageAnAgent. run_agent_slack_suite runs the retrieval cases against the agent through the REAL Slack transport (threads in C0BQH5S6P1P; tool calls captured from sub-workflow executions). Suites run synchronously, write results to the shared testing Supabase project, and post reports to Slack; prefer one run at a time. get_darwin_messages lists initial Slack messages that involve Darwin (no replies, eval channels excluded); get_darwin_session fetches one thread's messages. Both are read-only.

parameters.description: Runs the Darwin integration test suite (IntegrationRun). Executes every enabled case in integration_cases through the agent, evaluates assertions, writes integration_results, and posts a summary to Slack (#C09DRCJLQCE). Runs synchronously — a full run takes 2-5 minutes. Returns the Slack post result. Input: requested_by (who or what asked for the run).

parameters.description: Runs the Darwin consistency eval suite (ConsistencyRun, pass^k). Each enabled case in consistency_cases asks Darwin the same question k times in isolated sessions; an LLM judge scores cross-attempt agreement; a case passes when at least min_consistent attempts agree. Writes consistency_attempts + consistency_results, posts a report to Slack (#C09DRCJLQCE). Runs synchronously — a full case takes 5-10 minutes. Inputs (optional): requested_by; slug (one case).

parameters.description: Lists every initial (thread-starting) Slack message that involves Darwin since a date, across all conversations the bot can read. Fast: scans channel history only, never fetches replies. Excludes eval channels (C0BQH5S6P1P, C09DRCJLQCE) and bot-authored noise. Returns one row per thread: month, ts, thread_ts, channel_id, channel_name, is_im, user, user_name (Slack display name; empty when lookup fails), kind ('initial' = a human asked Darwin directly; 'thread_with_bot' = Darwin replied inside a thread started by someone else or by a bot post — use get_darwin_session to see who asked), reply_count, text (120-char preview). Use get_darwin_session to drill into any thread. Inputs (all optional): oldest (YYYY-MM-DD, default 2026-07-25); bot_user_id (override env default); exclude_channels (extra CSV channel IDs).

Runs synchronously — a full run takes 3-10 minutes. Inputs: requested_by (required), category and slug (optional case filters).

parameters.description: Runs the FirstClassDarwin agent retrieval eval suite through the REAL Slack transport (AgentSlackRun). Each case posts as Rob @mentioning the agent in a Slack thread; the dispatch waits for the bot reply, captures tool calls from tool sub-workflow executions via parentAgentRun.threadId, scores with the same retrieval scorer, and writes retrieval_results with mechanism='agent-slack', agent='firstclassdarwin', plus duration_ms. Posts the run summary to Slack (#C0BQH5S6P1P). Runs synchronously — a full run takes 10-30 minutes; one case 2-5 minutes. Note: node tools (get_session, get_project, firecrawl) are invisible to this capture — workflow tools only. Inputs: requested_by (required); category and slug (optional case filters); channel_id (optional, default C0BQH5S6P1P).
